problem: Existing methods that store foundation-model features in 3D scenes (point clouds, voxels/TSDF, neural fields) rely on projecting 2D features into 3D. This causes projection errors and yields heavy representations. LM-Nav stores only semantic features and AnyLoc only localization features, and neither gives an efficient way to build the data structure.
motivation: Robots need compact, scalable spatial understanding that supports both language and image interaction in large scenes. Keeping foundation-model features attached to their original view poses avoids reprojection heuristics. Poses are also guaranteed valid navigation goals, and view redundancy can be exploited for robust localization.
key_idea: Represent a 3D scene as a sparse pose graph whose nodes hold foundation-model embeddings (CLIP for semantics, PCA-VLAD-DINOv2 for localization), built by sampling one pose per cell of a 5D position and orientation grid.
insight: Storing per-view embeddings instead of projecting them into 3D gives a few-MB scene representation of only a few thousand poses, while view redundancy makes bundle voting effective. The ablation on ScanNet shows that larger bundles, a moderate Gaussian sigma, dataset-specific VLAD vocabularies and higher PCA dimensions all help; a too-large sigma favors outliers, and bundle size trades off against latency. Bundle voting alone gives +17.5 coarse R@1 on ScanNet, and ICP refinement adds to it mainly for fine accuracy.
method: 5D grid sampling: cells over (x,y,z) with resolution dl plus spherical yaw/pitch partitioning (dθ, dφ, with θ divisions per ring scaled by cos). Each cell is hashed by keys (i,j,k,l,m) and stores one pose and its embeddings.

Efficient construction: iterate over the trajectory keeping a cell-centering score. When the pose exits a cell, compute embeddings only for the best-centered image. A 10 s revisit threshold prevents excessive updates.

Dual features: OpenCLIP ViT-L/14 (DataComp-1B), 768-d float16, for semantics. AnyLoc-style DINOv2 ViT-g/14 layer-31 value features with a 32-center VLAD (32768-d), PCA-compressed to 512-d, with dataset-specific vocabulary and PCA, for localization.

Text and image queries: cosine similarity search with FAISS between the query embedding and pose embeddings. An LLM extracts the query from the user command. Image queries use the localization features only.

Disambiguation and navigation: several top candidates are checked for FOV overlap. If they do not overlap, the user is asked for clarification. Stored poses serve as valid navigation goals or waypoints in a teach-and-repeat style.

Bundle re-localization with Spatial Gaussian Voting: aggregate K_b=15 odometry-linked query poses, retrieve K_c=5 candidates each, realign them to the middle pose, and sum Gaussians in 5D (σxyz 0.45 m ScanNet / 2.2 m KITTI, σθφ 20°). The highest vote gives the pose and a confidence score.
Optional ICP refinement: when a mesh and depth are available, each candidate is refined by ICP before voting.

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark is evaluated. Text queries, disambiguation and language navigation are shown only qualitatively (figure and video). Table 1 gives EPG size and redundancy statistics.
results: EPG simple slightly beats AnyLoc on ScanNet (coarse R@1 73.5 vs 71.6) and KITTI (77.0 vs 75.8). Bundle voting raises coarse R@1 to 90.0 on ScanNet and 89.0 on KITTI. ICP-bundle on ScanNet reaches 91.0 coarse and 79.0 fine R@1. The whole multi-scene EPG is only about 2.5–14.7 MB.
limitations: The pose graph is built offline from given poses. It is not integrated with SLAM optimization or real-time updates.

Localization of queried objects is approximate (a pose and direction, not precise 3D), and short-range perception is still needed. Language navigation and the text tasks are evaluated only qualitatively.
The bundle method needs the robot to move first, which adds latency. ICP refinement needs a mesh and depth, and coarse initial poses can make ICP fail.
